content: अङ्गम् [अम् गत्यादौ बा˚-गन्; according to <ls>Nir.</ls> अङ्ग, अङ्गनात् अञ्चनात् वा] .²1 The body. .²2 A limb or member of the body; शेषाङ्गनिर्माणविधौ विधातुः <ls>Ku. 1. 33</ls>; क्लेशस्याङ्गमदत्वा <ls>Pt. 5. 32</ls> without undergoing troubles; इति स्वप्नोपमान्मत्वा कामान्मा गास्तदङ्गताम् . <ls>Ki. 11. 34</ls> do not be influenced or swayed by them (do not be subject to them) .²3 ({%a%}) A division or department (of anything), a part or portion, as of a whole; as सप्ताङ्गम् राज्यम्, चतुरङ्गम् बलम्, चतुःषष्ट्यङ्गम् ज्योतिःशास्त्रम् see the words; गीताङ्गानाम् <ls>Pt. 5. 56</ls>; यज्ञश्चेत्प्रतिरुद्धःस्यादेकेनाङ्गेन यज्वनः <ls>Ms. 11. 11</ls>. (Hence) ({%b%}) A supplementary or auxiliary portion, supplement; षडङ्ग or साङ्ग वेदः A peculiar use of the word अङ्ग in masculine gender may here be noted वेदांश्चैव तु वेदाङ्गान् वेदान्तानि तथा स्मृतीः . अधीत्य ब्राह्मणः पूर्वं शक्तितोऽन्यांश्च संपठेत् <ls>Bṛhadyogiyājñavalkya Smṛti 12. 34</ls>. ({%c%}) A constituent part, essential requisite or component; सर्वैर्बलाङ्गैः <ls>R. 7. 59</ls>; तदङ्गमग्र्यं मघवन् महाक्रतो <ls>R. 3. 46</ls>. ({%d%}) An attributive or secondary part; secondary, auxiliary or dependent member (serving to help the principal one) (<ab>opp.</ab> प्रधान or अङ्गिन्); अङ्गी रौद्ररसस्तत्र सर्वेऽङ्गानि रसाः पुनः <ls>S. D. 517</ls>; अत्र स्वभावोक्तिरुत्प्रेक्षांङ्गम् <ls>Malli.</ls> on <ls>Ki. 8. 26</ls>. ({%e%}) An auxiliary means or expedient (प्रधानोपयोगी उपायः or उपकरणम्); सर्वकार्यशरीरेषु मुक्त्वाङ्गस्कन्धपञ्चकम् . मन्त्रो योध इवाधीर सर्वाङ्गैः संबृतैरपि .. <ls>Śi. 2. 28-29</ls>; see अङ्गाङ्गि, पञ्चाङ्ग also ({%the angas%} of the several sciences or departments of knowledge will be given under those words). .²4 (<ab>Gram.</ab>). A name for the base of a word; यस्मात्प्रत्ययविधिस्तदादिप्रत्यये अङ्गम् <ls>P. I. 4. 13</ls>; यः प्रत्ययो यस्मात्क्रियते तदादिशब्दस्वरूपं तस्मिन्प्रत्यये परे अङ्गसंज्ञं स्यात् <ls>Sk.</ls> The अङ्ग terminations are those of the nominative, and accusative singular and dual. .²5 (Drama) ({%a%}) One of the sub-divisions of the five joints or sandhis in dramas; the मुख has 12, प्रतिमुख 13, गर्भ 12, विमर्ष 13 and उपसंहार 14, the total number of the {%angas%} being thus 64; for details see the words. ({%b%}) The whole body of subordinate characters. .²6 (<ab>astr.</ab>) A name for the position of stars (लग्न). See अङ्गाधीश. .²7 A symbolical expression for the number six (derived from the six Vedāngas). .²8 The mind; हिरण्यगर्भाङ्गभुवं मुनिं हरिः <ls>Śi. 1. 1</ls>; see अङ्गज also. .²9 <ab>N.</ab> of the chief sacred texts of the jainas. .{@-ङ्गः@} (<ab>pl.</ab>) <ab>N.</ab> of a country and the people inhabiting it, the country about the modern Bhāgalpur in Bengal. [It lay on the south of Kauśikī Kachchha and on the right bank of the Ganges. Its capital was Champā, sometimes called Aṅgapurī, Lomapādapurī, Karṇapurī or Mālinī. According to Daṇḍin (अङ्गेषु गङ्गातटे बहिश्चम्पायाः) and Hiouen Thsang it stood on the Ganges about 24 miles west of a rocky island. General Cunningham has shown that this description applies to the hill opposite Pātharghāṭā, that it is 24 miles east of Bhāgalpur, and that there are villages called Champanagar and Champapura adjoining the last. According to Sanskrit poets the country of the Aṅgas lay to the east of Girivraja, the capital of Magadha and to the north-east or south-east of Mithilā. The country was in ancient times ruled by Karṇa] <ab>cf.</ab> अङ्गं गात्रान्तिकोपाय प्रतीकेष्वप्रधानके . देशभेदे तु पुंसि स्यात् … .. <ls>Nm.</ls> {%a.%} .²1 Contiguous. .²2 Having members or divisions.
